findings.text: non-blocking: the identity early-return in _cached_stream_entry ignores the new whole flag, so a whole-stream caller is handed a tail-only entry when the cache holds one. Reproduced at the head tree: a 43-record stream read once, its events cache cleared, three records appended, cached_stream_events(path) returning the 3 growth records at cursor offset 6680, then cached_stream_events(path, whole=True) returned the same 3 records rather than 43 (logs/probe-whole-entry-head.log). Every production caller passes whole=True (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1197, reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:837, reckon/_backends.py:4117, 4154, 4629) and the docstring at reckon/_backends.py:3847 promises a whole read when the cache no longer holds the stream, so a default-path caller anywhere in the process makes those scans answer over a tail; it is latent only because no production caller takes the default path today, and _stream_summary:4038 builds a summary from whatever that early return yields.

non-blocking: _StreamCursor.covers is added and never called; `git grep .covers(` over the head tree's reckon and tests returns nothing, so the class carries a fourth identity comparison beside grows_from and identity that no reader uses and no test exercises.

non-blocking: the caller-carried resume branch in _observe_run_stream dropped the base revision's `offset <= size` guard and now resumes on _stream_head_intact alone, so a resume whose offset is past the end of a truncated stream seeks past EOF and returns the carried state with an unchanged offset instead of the whole-stream read observe_log:4535 still documents. I probed it at head (219,000-byte stream truncated to 21,900 with the 8 KiB recorded opening intact, resume offset 219,000): the offset came back 21,900 with PAST_EOF False, because _summarised_observation answers before this branch, so the guard's absence is shielded by the summary path today rather than exercised.

non-blocking: the live figure 157.3 MB -> 2.4 MB -> 1.4 MB is attributed to cached_stream_events, but it can only have been taken on the new default (non-whole) path, and every production call site passes whole=True (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1197, reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:837, reckon/_backends.py:4629), while the tick itself reaches the cache through _summarised_observation and the unchanged _STREAM_SUMMARIES resume. The table therefore does not show the reader s13 censused (reckon/_backends.py:_cached_stream_entry at 42.7 % of a tick's bytes) moving, and the station's own parsed-byte count may not follow the table; the prose at line 566-572 already declines to claim the after-window result, but the first two rows are read as that reader's cost.

non-blocking: the sibling test's exact-equality guard was loosened to a suffix check (assert events == whole[len(whole) - len(events):]) plus `malformed == 0`, so a cache that answers a stale prefix ending at the right length, or drops the appended record and returns an empty list, still passes; the assertion no longer fails on the regression it was written for, only on an answer that is not a suffix of the file at all.
